newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds quiet, focus on Treasury auction.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds quiet, focus on Treasury auction.

text.p: A U.S. Treasury auction as well as a temporary lack of new corporate bond supply, kept most investors out of the U.S. corporate bond market on Tuesday, traders said.

In the high-grade market, a Teasury auction of $17 billion in three-year notes put a lid on corporate bond trading for most of the day, traders said. High-grade bond spreads ended the day unchanged on low volume, they added.
Traders noted investors will typically avoid buying corporate bonds prior to an auction in order to avoid potential volatility in the Treasury market.
In the high-yield bond market, a temporary dearth of new corporate bond issues left most investors on the sidelines.
"Buyers are flush with cash and they're not about to sell their bonds. So people have been looking to the new issue market to invest," said one trader.
French Fragrances Inc, a Miami, Florida-based fragrance manufacturer, sold $115 million in junk bonds on Tuesday, the only high-yield offering of the day.
The deal, which was increased from an original size of $100 million, was underwriten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
The B2/B-plus-rated notes priced to yield 10 3/8 percent.
Prices in the overall high-yield market were unchanged to 1/8 of a point lower on Tuesday, a trader said. Volume was particularly light.
While the forward calendar for high-yield offerings is rapidly building, only four new deals for a total of approximately $700 million are expected for this week.
Elsewhere, Coleman Holdings Inc announced that it planned to redeem roughly $281 million in senior secured discount notes (face value) by sometime in July.
The news drove the price of the bonds to 92 from around 90, traders said.
